h1:
Roi Et Breakfast
Eat Like a Local, From the Morning Market to Lakeside Coffee
intro: Breakfast in Roi Et comes in more flavors than you'd expect. Get up early and walk the market for fragrant grilled rice (khao jee) and sticky rice with pork skewers; want something warm and brothy, and there's rice porridge, congee, khanom jeen, pan eggs, even chicken rice by the lake. Sleep in a little and you can just sip coffee beside Bueng Phlan Chai. We've rounded up what locals actually eat for breakfast, where to find it, which shops in which areas, what time they open, and roughly what it costs — focused on places that are genuinely open and where locals really go.

blocks.html: Roi Et is an early-rising town. The markets start setting up before the sky lightens, and once the morning warms up a bit the rice porridge, congee, khanom jeen, and pan-egg shops open one after another. The cafes around Bueng Phlan Chai get busy from mid-morning to noon. The nice thing about breakfast here is that it's cheap and the local dishes are still easy to find. If you're visiting Roi Et and want to start the day the way locals do, this article walks you from morning-market snacks to sit-down shops and lakeside coffee.

blocks.text: What Locals Eat for Breakfast in Roi Et

blocks.html: Breakfast for people in Roi Et roughly splits into two camps. The first is market food you eat on the move — bag it up and go: khao jee (grilled sticky rice), sticky rice with pork skewers, sticky rice with custard, grilled snacks. The second is hot food you sit down for: rice porridge, congee, khanom jeen, pan eggs, and chicken rice. Coffee and cafes came later but hit hard in Roi Et — the town has so many cafes it's nicknamed the city of a hundred cafes.

items: Market food on the go — khao jee, sticky rice with pork skewers, sticky rice with custard, pa thong ko (Chinese doughnuts), grilled snacks; bag it and eat as you walk
Hot sit-down food — rice porridge, congee, khanom jeen, pan eggs, chicken rice, Vietnamese kuay jab; good if you want something warm and brothy
Coffee and cafes — from old-school market coffee to lakeside cafes by Bueng Phlan Chai; an easy, relaxed way to start the day

blocks.text: Market Breakfast — Khao Jee, Pork Skewers, Sticky Rice

blocks.html: If you want a real Isan-style breakfast scene, start at the morning market. Wander a bit and you'll find stalls grilling fragrant khao jee, hot sticky rice paired with pork skewers, and plenty of other grilled morning snacks. It's all very cheap, so you can try several things in one meal.

items: Khao jee — sticky rice pressed onto a skewer, salted, and grilled until the surface goes crisp and fragrant, then brushed with egg and grilled again until golden. A morning favorite you'll find at almost every market, around ฿10–25 per skewer.

Sticky rice with pork skewers — marinated grilled pork on skewers, eaten with hot sticky rice wrapped in banana leaf or bagged. A quick, portable breakfast that fills you up fast. Pork skewers run about ฿10–12 each, sticky rice ฿10 a bag.

Sticky rice with custard / grilled sticky rice — the sweet option, often sold at the same stalls as khao jee. Coconut sticky rice with custard, or grilled sticky rice with banana filling wrapped in banana leaf.
Pa thong ko & soy milk — the classic morning pairing with coffee, found all over town. Hot fried pa thong ko dipped in soy milk or custard.

blocks.title: Want it fresh? Go a little earlier
blocks.html: The well-known khao jee and pork-skewer stalls at the morning markets grill fresh one skewer at a time and often sell out before mid-morning. If you're after hot-off-the-grill, aim to hit the market around 6:00–8:00 AM for the freshest options and the best selection.

blocks.text: Morning Markets Worth Walking in Roi Et Town

blocks.html: Roi Et has several morning markets spread across town and the outskirts, each with a slightly different vibe. Here's our ranking of the markets where you can actually find good breakfast food and walk around easily.

items.name: Rung Charoen Morning Market (town center)
items.blurb: The main morning market for Roi Et locals, open before dawn. Fresh produce, bagged local snacks, and morning grill stalls all in one place — khao jee, sticky rice with pork skewers, fried snacks, sweets. It's the easiest starting point if you want to sample several breakfast dishes in one spot, and it's close to Bueng Phlan Chai so you can walk on from here.
items.meta: Town center, near Bueng Phlan Chai · open pre-dawn to mid-morning

items.name: Thung Mong Market / Night-into-Dawn Market
items.blurb: A lively market area that runs from evening into late night and carries on through the pre-dawn hours. It's a hub for all kinds of food and home to several old-school rice porridge shops. Good for very early risers or for anyone who wants a late-night meal that rolls into breakfast — plenty of savory and sweet to choose from.

items.name: Ban Non Sawang Morning Market (Nuea Mueang subdistrict)
items.blurb: A community morning market in the Nuea Mueang area, with a homey neighborhood feel where locals come to shop for ingredients and grab breakfast. It's a place to see real local morning life — khao jee, sticky rice, grilled snacks, and native vegetables. Good if you want to get away from the in-town markets.
items.meta: Nuea Mueang subdistrict, just outside town · mornings

items.name: Rajabhat Front Market (university area)
items.blurb: A market by Roi Et Rajabhat University with lots of student-priced snacks — grilled food, fried snacks, hot sticky rice, and drinks. Good if you want a light bite on a budget and just want to graze as you walk.
items.meta: Rajabhat area · runs on market days

blocks.text: Rice Porridge, Congee, Pan Eggs — the Hot Sit-Down Crowd

blocks.html: If you'd rather skip the market and sit down for a relaxed meal, Roi Et has sit-down breakfast spots that locals go to regularly — from Chinese-style rice porridge to pan eggs, congee, and Vietnamese kuay jab. We've picked the places that are genuinely open and that locals talk about often.

items.name: Pak Mo-Phu Phan (Vietnamese breakfast)
items.blurb: A Vietnamese-style breakfast spot that Roi Et locals talk about a lot — Vietnamese kuay jab, steamed rice-flour rolls, pan eggs, Vietnamese bread, and strong Vietnamese coffee, all made fresh. Good if you want several breakfast dishes in one place; comfortable seating with parking.

items.name: Aew Pan Eggs
items.blurb: A go-to pan-egg shop open mornings only. Hot pan eggs come in a small skillet with Vietnamese pork sausage, sausage, and ham, eaten with toast and coffee — a simple breakfast that fills you up just right. Mornings to mid-morning only, so go too late and it may already be closed.

items.name: Khun Or Breakfast House
items.blurb: A mixed-menu breakfast spot open from before dawn — pan eggs, rice porridge, fried rice, fried snacks, bread, and hot drinks. Good for families or groups where everyone wants something different. Open through the early afternoon.

items.name: Liang Heng Rice Porridge
items.blurb: An old-school Chinese-style plain rice porridge shop that locals know well, over by the night-into-dawn market area. Lots of side dishes to order — salted black beans with minced pork, stir-fried morning glory, braised bamboo pith — eaten with genuinely hot rice porridge. This place is bigger in the evening-to-late-night crowd than at breakfast, but if you want real Chinese-style porridge in Roi Et, this is the one to try.
items.meta: Night-market area · best in the evening to late night

items.name: Jok Hong Te (Congee)
items.blurb: The congee shop Roi Et locals recommend when you want something light and warm. Pork congee with egg, liver, and offal as you like, topped with shredded ginger and spring onion. Good if your stomach's a bit off or you just want something easy to eat in the morning. Check the opening hours of each branch with the shop before you go.
items.meta: In town · check opening hours with the shop

items.name: First Chicken Rice by the Lake
items.blurb: A chicken rice shop in the Bueng Phlan Chai lakeside area, open from morning through evening. Fragrant chicken rice, tender chicken, and a punchy dipping sauce — good if you want a proper rice plate for a more substantial breakfast. It's near the lake so you can stroll afterward, and a solid choice if you sleep in and the market's already done.
items.meta: Bueng Phlan Chai lakeside · roughly 6:00 AM–9:00 PM

blocks.title: Check opening hours before you go
blocks.html: Many breakfast shops in Roi Et open only from morning to early afternoon, and some have different closing days. The times we've listed are rough ranges based on the latest info. If you're set on a particular shop, call or check its page before heading out to be sure — especially the ones that are bigger in the evening, like Liang Heng Rice Porridge.

blocks.text: Khanom Jeen — the True Isan Breakfast You Shouldn't Miss

blocks.html: Khanom jeen (fermented rice noodles) is a popular breakfast and late-morning meal for Isan folk. Soft noodles topped with a curry sauce, then piled with fresh and pickled vegetables to taste. In Roi Et the sauces you'll see most are nam ya pa (herbal jungle curry), nam ya kati (coconut curry), and Isan-style fermented-fish curry. Some shops let you mix several sauces on one plate.

items: Nam ya pa — a clear, coconut-free curry, hot and herbal; the true Isan style locals love
Nam ya kati — a rich, sweet, creamy coconut curry, milder and good if you don't want it too spicy
Loaded sides — fresh vegetables, bean sprouts, lemon basil, pickles, chili powder, lime; scoop your own to taste. Isan khanom jeen is all about piling on the veg.
Khanom Jeen Baan Khun Ya — an in-town khanom jeen shop people talk about, with several sauces to choose from and other dishes on the side. Good if you want to make a proper meal of it.

blocks.title: Eat khanom jeen the Isan way
blocks.html: Isan folk like khanom jeen with sides like fried chicken, pork crackling, or fried fish balls, plus a big pile of fresh and pickled vegetables. Try scooping a few different sauces onto one plate — you'll get a rounder flavor, the way locals eat it here.

blocks.text: Morning Coffee and Lakeside Cafes by Bueng Phlan Chai

blocks.html: Roi Et is known for having so many cafes that people jokingly call it the city of a hundred cafes. If you sleep in and want a relaxed start to the day, the Bueng Phlan Chai lakeside area has several cafes with lake views — sip coffee while watching the Hor Vote tower and the water. And for old-school coffee, you can still find it at the markets and old shops around town.

items.name: SAO CAFE
items.blurb: A newer lakeside cafe by Bueng Phlan Chai with a great setting and views of the Hor Vote tower. Big drinks and food menu, open from morning to evening — good for an early start or a long sit.

items.name: Psycho Coffee Roasters-101
items.blurb: A serious-coffee cafe in Roi Et that roasts its own beans. Good for anyone who likes a bold cup and wants to start the day strong.

items.name: Chao Cafe Lakeside
items.blurb: Another Bueng Phlan Chai lakeside cafe with chill seating and water views. Good for photos and a relaxed morning before walking around the lake.

items.name: Old-School Market Coffee
items.blurb: The traditional camp, found at the morning markets and old shops. Hot old-style coffee with pa thong ko, cheap the way a local breakfast should be.

blocks.title: Want the lake view in the morning?
blocks.html: Bueng Phlan Chai is pleasant in the morning before the crowds. You can walk a lap around the lake for exercise, then stop at a lakeside cafe afterward — it works out nicely. But most lakeside cafes open around 7 AM, so if you're up earlier, grab market food at the nearby Rung Charoen Morning Market first, then come back for coffee once the cafes open.

blocks.text: How to Plan a Roi Et Breakfast That Just Works

blocks.html: If you've only got one morning and want to hit all the Roi Et breakfast highlights, try this timing. You'll get market food, hot sit-down dishes, and lakeside coffee all in one morning.

blocks.label: One Morning, Everything
blocks.title: Up Early for the Market, Then Hot Food and Lakeside Coffee

items.note: Grab khao jee, sticky rice with pork skewers, and grilled snacks in a bag to nibble while you browse the fresh produce.
Pick one — pan eggs at Aew Pan Eggs, Vietnamese kuay jab at Pak Mo-Phu Phan, or lakeside chicken rice.
Walk it off, photograph the Hor Vote tower, and wait for the lakeside cafes to open.
Sip coffee with a lake view at SAO CAFE or Chao Cafe to cap off a relaxed breakfast.

blocks.label: The Khanom Jeen Route
blocks.title: A Light Morning Focused on Khanom Jeen and Coffee

items.note: Head to Khanom Jeen Baan Khun Ya, try both nam ya pa and nam ya kati, and pile on the fresh and pickled veg.
Stop for sticky rice with custard or pa thong ko to take with you if you're still hungry.
Follow up with lakeside coffee or old-school coffee in town to start the day at an unhurried pace.

faq.q: Where should I start a Roi Et breakfast?
faq.a: For a local feel, start at Rung Charoen Morning Market in the town center — you can grab khao jee, sticky rice with pork skewers, and grilled snacks all in one walk, then follow up with a hot sit-down meal or coffee by Bueng Phlan Chai nearby. It's a convenient starting point where you can try several things in one morning.

faq.q: Where do I go for rice porridge or congee in the morning in Roi Et?
faq.a: For real Chinese-style plain rice porridge, Liang Heng Rice Porridge by the night-market area is the old establishment locals know — though it's bigger in the evening-to-late-night crowd than at breakfast. For congee, try Jok Hong Te, and a mixed-menu breakfast spot like Khun Or Breakfast House also serves rice porridge. We'd suggest checking opening hours with the shop before you go.

faq.q: What time do breakfast shops in Roi Et open?
faq.a: Most hot sit-down spots open around 6:00 AM — for example, Pak Mo-Phu Phan (roughly 6:00 AM–2:00 PM) and Khun Or Breakfast House (roughly 5:30 AM–2:00 PM). Pan-egg shops like Aew Pan Eggs open mornings only, roughly 6:00–11:00 AM. The morning markets start even earlier, before the sky lightens. These are rough ranges, so check with the shop to be sure.

faq.q: What kinds of khanom jeen sauce does Roi Et have?
faq.a: In Roi Et you'll most often find nam ya pa (a clear, coconut-free curry that's spicy and herbal, Isan style) and nam ya kati (a rich, sweet, creamy coconut curry that's milder). Some shops also have fermented-fish curry. Eat it with fresh vegetables, bean sprouts, pickles, and chili powder — try scooping several sauces onto one plate for the rounded flavor locals go for.

faq.q: Can I still find breakfast in Roi Et if I sleep in?
faq.a: Yes. If the morning market has wound down, there are still shops open through the early afternoon, like Pak Mo-Phu Phan, Khun Or Breakfast House, and the lakeside chicken rice that stays open into the evening. Most lakeside cafes by Bueng Phlan Chai open around 7 AM through the evening, so you can comfortably start a late breakfast with coffee and a light bite.
